problem:
Find the Laplace transform of $y(t),$ if 

$$
{y}^{″}+2y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(0)=0,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Second-Order ODEs Using Laplace Transforms

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}-3{y}^{′}+2y} & =L{6{e}^{-t}} \\ L{{y}^{″}}-3L{{y}^{′}}+2L{y} & =6L{{e}^{-t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce $L{y}=Y(s).$

To calculate $L{{y}^{′}}$ and $L{{y}^{″}},$  we use formulas for the Laplace transforms of the derivatives and apply the initial conditions:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{′}} & =sY(s)-y(0)=sY(s) \\ L{{y}^{″}} & ={s}^{2}Y(s)-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)={s}^{2}Y(s)-3\end{aligned}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L{{e}^{-t}}=\frac{1}{s+1}
$$

Therefore, we can solve for $Y(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}}-3L{{y}^{′}}+2L{y} & =6L{{e}^{-t}} \\ ({s}^{2}Y(s)-3)-3(sY(s))+2Y(s) & =6(\frac{1}{s+1}) \\ ({s}^{2}-3s+2)Y(s) & =3+\frac{6}{s+1} \\ (s-1)(s-2)Y(s) & =\frac{3s+9}{s+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3(s+3)}{(s+1)(s-1)(s-2)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3(s+3)}{({s}^{2}-1)(s-2)}\end{aligned}
$$
